chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ali bin Hassan, from Musa bin Bakr, from Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said:
Kindness (or gentleness) is half of life.

key_terms.الرِّفْقُ: Kindness, gentleness, or ease in conduct
key_terms.الْعَيْشِ: Life, livelihood, or way of living

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of kindness (rifq) in Shia Islamic ethics?
ai.summary: In this concise hadith from al-Kafi, Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) identifies 'rifq' (gentleness and ease) as half of one's livelihood, highlighting its pivotal role in spiritual and worldly success. This teaching aligns with the Shia emphasis on *akhlaq* (character) as a means of facilitating divine grace, suggesting that a gentle disposition not only eases interpersonal relations but also opens the door to sustenance and contentment.
